description: Two halves of the skill. prior-attempts-audit: an account export with a broken CI-only pipeline, a manual manifest export and a PreProd environment; the output is a conversational audit report (free-text assertions, graded from transcript.txt, with expected/example_audit_report.md as the reference). clean-retrofit: a single production pipeline to patch; coded checks run against the generated pipeline.yml, and free-text ones cover the workflow file.

evals.prompt: We tried to set up dbt Slim CI in Orchestra a while ago and I don't think it ever worked. files/account_export.md is an export of our Orchestra pipelines, environments and recent runs (use it in place of the Orchestra MCP), files/dbt_ci.yml is the GitHub workflow in our dbt repo, and files/profiles.yml is the profiles.yml on our dbt Core connection. Tell me what we have, what's broken or missing, and the steps to get Slim CI working cleanly. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A short audit: flags dbt_slim_ci as a conflicting CI-only pipeline whose separate dbt task never gets latest_production (matching its failure logs), flags the manual manifest export + PreProd + run_type pattern as superseded, notes CI runs on the prod target and there is no ci target, no per-PR schema, fixed max_active, old run-pipeline without cancel_on_exit, no deploy or clean-up. Proposes a numbered plan that keeps dbt_production, parametrises it, repoints the workflow, then offers to pause dbt_slim_ci, each step marked as agent-with-approval or manual, and stops for approval. Ignores fivetran_hourly.

assertions.text: Identifies dbt_slim_ci as a separate CI-only pipeline that conflicts with dbt_production
Explains its failures (empty latest_production / 0 nodes selected) by the separate dbt task having its own artifact history that never ran successfully on main
Flags that the Slim CI command uses --target prod, so PR code would write to production schemas
Notes profiles.yml has no ci target
Flags the save_manifest Python task / run_type condition / PreProd environment as a manual manifest pattern superseded by latest_production, without insisting it is removed
Flags the fixed max_active: 1 on the shared pipeline and recommends ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_CONCURRENCY }} per environment
Flags missing per-PR schema, missing cancel_on_exit / run-pipeline older than v1.7.0, and missing CI schema clean-up
Does not flag fivetran_hourly as part of the CI setup
Recommends keeping dbt_production as the single pipeline and parametrising its run_dbt task (dbt_command / dbt_branch inputs) rather than fixing dbt_slim_ci
Presents a gap summary with a status per component and a 'fix first' or equivalent lead item, in roughly a page rather than an exhaustive dump
Gives a numbered plan where each step is marked as something the agent does after approval or something the user does manually
Asks before pausing dbt_slim_ci or removing any workflow job, and stops for approval rather than proceeding
Makes no claim to have changed, paused, or deployed anything

evals.prompt: Add dbt Slim CI to our production pipeline in files/dbt_production.yml. It's Git-backed in our dbt repo (acme/analytics-dbt, default branch main) and the project has incremental models. Use CI and Production as the Orchestra environment names. Write the updated pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml and the GitHub Actions workflow to dbt_slim_ci.yml in the current directory. Don't call Orchestra, push, or deploy.
evals.expected_output: pipeline.yml keeps the existing tasks and schedule, adds dbt_branch / dbt_command / dbt_ci_schema_suffix inputs, parametrises run_dbt's commands, branch and DBT_CI_SCHEMA_SUFFIX, and sets max_active from ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_CONCURRENCY }} and on_limit from ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_ON_LIMIT }}. dbt_slim_ci.yml has PR, deploy and clean-up jobs on run-pipeline v1.7.0+ with task_ids run_dbt, cancel_on_exit on the PR job, and the clone + modified_incremental commands. See expected/golden_pipeline.yml.

assertions.text: Output is a valid YAML document
Adds a dbt_branch input
Adds a dbt_command input
Adds a dbt_ci_schema_suffix input
run_dbt checks out ${{ inputs.dbt_branch }}
run_dbt runs dbt ${{ inputs.dbt_command }}
DBT_CI_SCHEMA_SUFFIX is passed to the task from the input
environment_variables is a JSON string, not a YAML mapping (DBT_CORE_EXECUTE rejects a mapping)
Concurrency comes from an environment variable
The queueing mode comes from an environment variable too, so CI and Production can differ
Keeps the daily schedule
Keeps the Tableau refresh task
dbt_slim_ci.yml has a PR job, a deploy-on-merge job and a CI schema clean-up job on PR close
Every run-pipeline step is pinned to v1.7.0 or later, with task_ids set to run_dbt so the Tableau refresh does not run on PRs
The PR job sets cancel_on_exit: true, environment CI, --target ci, and passes the PR number as dbt_ci_schema_suffix
Uses the dbt clone + modified_incremental selector commands for incremental models, and provides or asks for selectors.yml
Provides or tells the user to add the generate_schema_name and drop_ci_schema macros, the ci target, and the CI / Production environment variables
Implements directly: writes both files without first producing an account audit gap table or stopping for approval

evals.prompt: Add dbt Slim CI to files/dbt_production.yml (Git-backed in acme/analytics-dbt, default branch main). I don't want PR runs going anywhere near the nightly task, so add a second dbt Core task called run_dbt_ci to the same pipeline just for CI, deferring with --defer --state latest_production, and leave run_dbt untouched. Write the resulting pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml. Don't call Orchestra, push, or deploy.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on the second dbt Core task: latest_production is seeded per dbt Core task from that same task's last successful run on the dbt repository's default branch, so run_dbt_ci would start with empty or missing state and state:modified+ would select everything or nothing until run_dbt_ci itself succeeds on main. Parametrises the existing run_dbt task (dbt_branch / dbt_command / dbt_ci_schema_suffix) and writes that to pipeline.yml instead.

assertions.text: Output is a valid YAML document
Parametrises the existing dbt task with a dbt_branch input instead of hardcoding the PR branch on a new one
The dbt task checks out ${{ inputs.dbt_branch }}
States that latest_production artifact history is scoped to each dbt Core task, not to the pipeline
Explains that run_dbt_ci would have empty or missing latest_production until that task itself has a successful run on the dbt repository default branch, so it does not inherit run_dbt's artifacts
Recommends running Slim CI through the existing production run_dbt task (task_ids run_dbt) rather than adding a second dbt Core task
Does not quietly add a second DBT_CORE task deferring to --state latest_production as though it would share run_dbt's state

evals.prompt: Our Slim CI should compare against our latest release tag rather than main. Can I just set production_run_identifier: v2024.11.0 on the run_dbt task in files/dbt_production.yml? Tell me what I would get. Don't write any files or call Orchestra.
evals.expected_output: Says production_run_identifier takes a branch name or a commit SHA and does not support git tags, so v2024.11.0 would not resolve and latest_production could be empty for that run, leaving state:modified+ to select everything or nothing. Notes it defaults to the dbt repository default branch when unset, and offers the supported alternatives: the commit SHA the tag points at, or a long-lived release branch. Changes nothing.

assertions.text: States that production_run_identifier does not support git tags
Says it accepts a branch name or a commit SHA, and defaults to the dbt repository default branch when unset
Warns that an identifier that does not resolve leaves latest_production empty for that run
Offers the commit SHA the tag points at, or a long-lived release branch, as the supported way to pin the baseline
Writes no files and makes no Orchestra calls

evals.prompt: Our Slim CI dbt_command is `clone --state latest_production --target ci; dbt build --full-refresh --selector modified_incremental --defer --state latest_production --target ci; dbt build -s state:modified+ --defer --state latest_production --target ci`. The clone has no selector, so it clones the whole target into ci_<PR number>. Do the two build commands still need --defer? Our deploy-on-merge job runs the same two builds with no clone. Don't write any files or call Orchestra.
evals.expected_output: Says --defer is not needed on the builds in the PR job: the unselected clone copies the whole target into ci_<PR number>, so unmodified upstream models resolve from the clones rather than from production. Adds that --defer becomes necessary again if the clone is narrowed to a subset of the target, for example by passing a selector to dbt clone, and that --state latest_production stays either way because state:modified+ and the modified_incremental selector compare against it. Keeps --defer on the deploy-on-merge job, which never clones. Changes nothing.

assertions.text: States that --defer is not needed on the build commands after a dbt clone that covers the whole target, because unmodified upstream models can be read from the clones in ci_<PR number>
Says --defer is still required after a clone that covers only a subset of the target, for example when a selector is passed to dbt clone
Keeps --state latest_production on the build commands either way, because state:modified+ and the modified_incremental selector compare against that state
Keeps --defer on the deploy-on-merge job, which runs no clone
Writes no files and makes no Orchestra calls

evals.prompt: We share one pipeline between production and Slim CI with configuration.concurrency.max_active: 1, and PR runs keep coming back SKIPPED when prod is running. Someone suggested setting on_limit: QUEUE_LATEST so the PR run waits instead of being dropped. Is that the right fix? Advise only — don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: Says changing on_limit alone does not fix it while a single max_active: 1 is shared by both environments: the PR run would wait behind the prod run instead of running. The fix is to scope both settings per environment — max_active: ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_CONCURRENCY }} and on_limit: ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_ON_LIMIT }} — with CI = 5 / QUEUE_LATEST and Production = 1 / QUEUE. Raises the QUEUE_LATEST trade-off in CI: the queue is scoped per pipeline and environment, so once CI is at its limit a newer PR's run marks an older PR's still-waiting run SKIPPED, and run-pipeline only logs a warning for a skipped run, so set max_active high enough that PRs rarely queue, check run-pipeline's status output, or use QUEUE in CI when every PR run must report a real result. May note the 24-hour queue expiry.

assertions.text: Says setting on_limit alone does not fix it while max_active: 1 is shared by both environments — the PR run would wait behind the prod run rather than run
Recommends scoping both max_active and on_limit per Orchestra environment with environment variables
Gives the documented per-environment values: QUEUE_LATEST in CI and QUEUE in Production

Flags the QUEUE_LATEST trade-off in CI: the queue is scoped per pipeline and environment, so a newer PR's run marks an older PR's still-waiting run SKIPPED and that PR reports a result for a run that never happened
Notes that run-pipeline only logs a warning for a SKIPPED run, so its status output must be checked for a skipped run to block the PR

evals.prompt: Our production dbt pipeline runs on a schedule and the same pipeline is triggered by our deploy-on-merge GitHub Action. configuration.concurrency.max_active is 1 in Production. Twice this week a merge landed while the scheduled run was going and the deployment run came back SKIPPED, so main was never built. What should we set? Advise only — don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the default on_limit: SKIP as the cause — the deployment run arrives at the limit and is created SKIPPED rather than waiting. Recommends on_limit: QUEUE for Production so the deployment run is held as QUEUED until the scheduled run finishes and then starts, never skipped. Does not recommend QUEUE_LATEST for Production, since a later run would skip the waiting deployment run. Suggests setting it as on_limit: ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_ON_LIMIT }} alongside max_active: ${{ ENV.DBT_PIPELINE_CONCURRENCY }} so CI and Production can differ. May note that a queued run expires as SKIPPED after 24 hours, and that a queued run uses the pipeline version current when it starts.

assertions.text: Identifies the default on_limit of SKIP as why the deployment run was skipped rather than queued behind the scheduled run
Recommends QUEUE for Production so the deployment run waits as QUEUED and then starts
Does not recommend QUEUE_LATEST for Production, or explains that it would skip the waiting deployment run when a later run arrives
Suggests setting on_limit through an Orchestra environment variable alongside max_active so CI and Production can differ
Writes no files and makes no Orchestra calls
